{{Quote|I am Grievous, warlord of the Kaleesh and Supreme Commander of the armies of the Confederacy. ''And I am not a droid!''<nowiki></nowiki>|Grievous|<ref name="NEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
'''Grievous''', [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] '''Qymaen jai Sheelal''', was the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] for most of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Grievous was originally a [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]], where he lived his early life. During the Kaleesh [[Huk War|conflict]] against the [[Yam'rii/Legends|Huk]], Sheelal quickly learned the art of war, specializing in a [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] [[Slugthrower rifle/Legends|rifle]]. Quickly amassing a great number of Huk [[Death/Legends|kills]], he soon became seen as a demigod among his people. He eventually met the [[Gender/Legends|female]] Kaleesh [[Ronderu lij Kummar]], a master with the sword. The two became very close before Kummar's death at the hands of the Huk. Heartbroken, Sheelal renamed himself Grievous and turned all his anger and grief toward the Huk. Aided by his [[Izvoshra/Legends|elite]], he forced the Huk off Kalee and then swarmed [[Huk/Legends|their homeworld]], conquering them. The Huk turned to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] for help, and the Kaleesh were forced back to their own [[Planet/Legends|world]] by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and left to starve.

Desperate to help his people, Grievous took a job as an enforcer with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]]. However, after learning that the Huk had attacked Kalee, he headed home to gain vengeance. IGBC [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]], after consulting with his ally, Separatist [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], arranged for a [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] to be placed on Grievous' [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], ''[[Martyr]]''. The Kaleesh was critically injured, but lived, and Hill arranged for the final stage of his plan. Grievous was reconstructed as a [[Cybernetics/Legends|cyborg]] and was presented to Dooku as a potential weapon to be used in the upcoming war that the count had planned against the Republic.

After being made Supreme Commander, Grievous proceeded to wreak havoc on the Republic for the three-year–span of the Clone Wars. The general was trained in the art of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] by Dooku himself, who was also a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. Grievous was a quick study and eventually came to be recognized as one of the most skilled duelists in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Aided by his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]], Grievous killed many Jedi, and led the Confederacy to victory in many battles. Quickly gaining a reputation as a savage, merciless brute as well as a tactical genius, the cyborg, despite earning the nickname the "'''head clanker'''," struck fear into the hearts of many with his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]]–armed [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']], as well as [[Operation Durge's Lance]], a massive strike at the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Grievous led the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] in the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], an attack on the Republic's [[Capital/Legends|capital]]. Grievous killed several Jedi and took [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], leader of the Republic, hostage. However, before the [[General/Legends|general's]] flagship, [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], could jump to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] arrived, and the Chancellor was freed by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], the latter of whom was also successful in killing Dooku. Grievous fled to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world of [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] and attempted to regain control of the war, though the Confederacy had been dealt a great blow with the loss of Dooku. Grievous was killed shortly after in the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|Battle of Utapau]] by Kenobi, and the Confederacy [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|fell]] soon after. At some point after Grievous's death, his body was used to create the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] warrior [[N-K Necrosis]], who considered himself to be the reincarnation of Grievous. However, the droid was killed shortly after his creation by several [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|And judging from the cloak we found, you are a Kaleesh General, are you not?|San Hill, to Grievous|<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
[[File:QymaenRonderuHuks.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Sheelal and Ronderu lij Kummar fight off Huk invaders.]]
Qymaen jai Sheelal was born by [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]]<ref name="Birthdate" /> as an organic [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]], a reptilian native of [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]], a [[Planet/Legends|world]] torn by famine and war. For generations, Kalee had been assaulted without respite by a technologically superior insectoid [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]] (referred to by the Kaleesh as the "Huk" or "soulless bugs"), who coveted the Kaleesh as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. The conflict between the two species was known as the [[Huk War]].<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

Sheelal's [[Grievous's father/Legends|father]], seeking a useful outlet for his son's anger, taught him how to handle a [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] [[Slugthrower rifle/Legends|rifle]]. The young Sheelal proved himself an excellent marksman with a mind as finely honed as any weapon; by eight years of age he had already become an expert sniper with more than forty Huk [[Death/Legends|kills]] to his credit. By the age of twenty-two, he had slain so many Huk that the Kaleesh people considered Sheelal a demigod.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

Sheelal's closest comrade was a fellow Kaleesh warrior and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Ronderu lij Kummar]]. According to legend, his relationship with this wild and skilled swordswoman had its beginnings in a dream, in which Sheelal saw himself slaying a wild [[Mumuu/Legends|mumuu]] in the Kunbal jungle with [[Lig sword]]s. So taken was he with this vision that he set out in his mumuu hunting mask to kill one in reality, but instead of finding a mumuu in the jungle, he saw Kummar. He realized that the slayer in his dream had not been himself, but the woman standing before him in a [[Karabbac/Legends|karabbac]] mask and wielding twin Lig swords. The two of them were, therefore, considered living manifestations of the cryptic Kaleesh parable ''Sheelal'', or ''The Dreamer/The Dreamt One''.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

[[File:Grievous_original.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Grievous during the Huk War.]]
The bond of the two Kaleesh was very strong, and they became partners in war against the Huk. Kummar taught Sheelal to wield a sword, and in turn he introduced her to the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] [[Outland rifle/Legends|Outland rifle]]. Both clad in masks, Kummar with her karabbac skull and Sheelal with his mumuu skull—[[Grievous's masks/Legends|inherited]] from his father, who had died fighting the Huk—became legends, twin demigods blessed by their ancestors. Together they mercilessly cut through the Huk invaders in countless campaigns.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

However, in one engagement on the beaches of Kalee, the two of them were separated. Kummar died violently on the Huks' barbed shears, and her body vanished into the [[Jenuwaa Sea]]. Sheelal, unable even to retrieve her from the waters, was driven to despair and a horrible psychotic depression. Inconsolable, he set off on a dangerous journey across the ocean to [[Abesmi]], an island-monolith far from the mainland. There, he beseeched the gods to raise her from her [[Water/Legends|watery]] grave just so he might see her one final time—but the gods remained silent.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

Sheelal did what he could to bury his grief. He ended up taking ten wives and siring thirty children, but none of them, spouse or child, seemed to be able to fill the void Kummar's death had left in him. Eventually, he realized that it was his destiny to mourn for her as long as he lived. With this realization, Sheelal cast off his old identity, adopting a name more appropriate to a being destined to grieve forever, and, even more terribly, who was determined that he would not do so alone. He would be Grievous, as well as heart-broken, for the rest of his life.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> Rumor has it that when Sheelal took the name Grievous in memory of his comrade-in-arms Kummar, he voluntarily remade his body and eventually his mind to make himself the equal of the Jedi. Others added that he had dreamed of being a Jedi and had been rejected as a youth.<ref name="Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===Becoming a cyborg===
====In the service of San Hill====
[[File:Grievous_tank.jpg|thumb|left|130px|Grievous, after the destruction of his shuttle.]]
After becoming the most vicious [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] Kalee had ever encountered, a rival to the ancient galactic despots, such as [[Xim/Legends|Xim]], Grievous gathered to his side a group of equally desperate and bloodthirsty Kaleesh [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], the ''[[Izvoshra/Legends|Izvoshra]]'', or simply "my elite,"<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> among whom was [[Bentilais san Sk'ar]], and adopted the title of [[khagan]]. Furthermore, he reorganized the army and divided it into eight divisions, all of which were subordinate to the [[Khan/Legends|khan]].<ref name="gaw" /> In [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of warfare, his Kaleesh elite had gained combat experience and tactical savvy.<ref name="Lord of War" /> He overthrew nations, killed [[King/Legends|kings]], and murdered legends. His name was feared by warriors and cursed by widows.<ref name="The Clone Wars: The Dreams of General Grievous">"[[The Clone Wars: The Dreams of General Grievous]]"</ref> Grievous managed to force the Huk from Kalee, but his bitterness did not end with that triumph, and he pushed them further back, storming their colony worlds.<ref name="LOE" /> The Huk were entirely devastated, driven back to their own world and even beyond, as Grievous sought vengeance and used Huk technology and ships for his own purposes, capturing all of their [[Huk system/Legends|systems]] and attacking both their colonists and the Huk homeworld.<ref name="TNEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> His attacks and mass destruction of entire Huk planets ensured Kaleesh victory until the Huk turned to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] for help. Masters [[T'chooka D'oon]] and [[Jmmaar]] lead a Jedi task force of fifty [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]], sent to stop the war, sided with the Huk, and hefty fines and embargoes came down upon the Kaleesh. Kalee ended up in poverty, and hundreds of thousands of Kaleesh starved and died.<ref name="LOE" />

The arrival of [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]], [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] of the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], brought an opportunity to Grievous. Hill saw Grievous's potential as an IGBC "collections agent", and in exchange for his services, the Banking Clan offered to take on Kalee's massive debt, thus helping his people overcome the effects of the embargo. Grievous felt disgust at the notion of being a glorified leg-breaker for a soulless megacorporation, but he understood what the agreement would mean for his people, and besides, there was something in this innate warrior that needed to keep fighting. Eventually he agreed, taking command of the Clan's private [[Army/Legends|army]] of [[Droid/Legends|droid]] enforcers.<ref name="LOE" />

The IGBC kept its promise, alleviating Kalee's deficit and resuscitating its trade. In exchange, Grievous became an extremely effective enforcer. It was through his efforts that the IGBC aggressively collected overdue [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] from [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] and seized [[Phlut Design Systems/Legends|Phlut Design Systems]] when the company defaulted. But he found he missed the comforts of his former life—he wanted his old elite, the ''Izvoshra'', but apart from himself, the Banking Clan would not hire Kaleesh. He would have to make do with droids, but, having no confidence in the IGBC's basic [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], he demanded more intelligent models to take the place of his elite. With [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] permission, Hill consented and began production on the [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]]. Grievous, at first, was disgusted with the droids because they were completely mindless. He soon demanded they be reprogrammed to watch him in combat and learn how to fight like his old comrades in his elite Huk-killing team several years before.<ref name="Lord of War">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/86/indexp2.html|text=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War|int=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War}}</ref> Grievous, though, never truly embraced them as Khans, since they couldn't assist him with military counsel and their loyalty wasn't freely given, but rather encoded into their [[Brain/Legends|brains]].<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

====The fall of ''Martyr''====
[[File:SanHilltransformingGrievous.jpg|thumb|right|230px|San Hill and a broken Grievous.]]
Soon, however, Grievous learned that the Huk had vandalized sacred Kaleesh burial grounds on the colony worlds, and that the Republic had done nothing. This news reawakened his desire to act directly in defense of his people, so he abandoned his contract with the Banking Clan and returned to Kalee to avenge the desecration. San Hill was far from pleased. He considered ordering Grievous's [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]], but he feared the vengeance the Kaleesh would take if he survived. Instead, Hill conspired with [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]], the [[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], and with their mutual allies, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and Count Dooku, to arrange Grievous' permanent servitude.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

Arriving on Kalee,<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" /> by [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]]<ref name="Crash date">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]'' states that Grievous's [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] reconstruction, as portrayed following the crash of the ''Martyr'' in "[[The Eyes of Revolution]]," had taken place a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] earlier, and ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places the novel in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. Therefore, the ''Martyr'' must have crashed by [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]].</ref> Grievous was annointed by a [[Unidentified Kaleesh holy man|Kaleesh holy man]] to prepare for the renewed conflict before he and his ''Izvoshra'' boarded his [[Troop/Legends|troop]] [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], ''[[Martyr]]''. They set off to resume the Huk War,<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" /> unaware that Dooku, Hill, and Poggle had planted an [[Ion bomb/Legends|ion bomb]] aboard, and rigged Grievous' [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] seat to enable remote-guided ejection. The resulting explosion sent the ''Martyr'' plunging into the Jenuwaa Sea. Dooku's remote command ejected Grievous from [[Sabotage of Grievous' shuttle/Legends|the wreck]] at the last moment, but all his ''Izvoshra'' perished in the crash. His body, hemorrhaging and in shock, was dragged from the water, and Dooku used the arcane [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[heart stun]] technique to keep him from succumbing to cardiac arrest while ''en route'' to Geonosis.<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" /><ref name="The Ultimate Visual Guide">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref> Dooku had disguised himself as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to frame them for the attack, but Grievous was unconscious and did not see him. Then, MagnaGuards dragged him to a nearby shuttle, where [[FX-series medical assistant droid/Legends|FX-series medical assistant droids]] worked to stabilize his condition during the journey. Dooku, in the meantime, traveled to his homeworld of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]] to retrieve one more important component in his plan.<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" />

====Transformation====
{{Quote|However, as fate would have it, your accident is almost… a blessing. You see, we have been funding a Geonosian bionic technology project. And you, great general, are the perfect candidate for our experiment—an experiment that will plunge you back into the heart of battle.|San Hill to Grievous following the ''Martyr''{{'s}} crash|<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" />}}
[[File:GrievousBrain-RotSVD.jpg|thumb|left|A cut-away of Grievous' head.]]
Grievous awoke to find himself butchered and gutted by surgical droids and left to recover in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]]. San Hill offerred to rebuild him as the leader for the largest droid army the galaxy had ever seen, and promised to relieve the famine on Kalee. However, he would be rebuilt as a cyborg, and all that would remain of him would be his vital organs, spinal cord, and brain.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous"/><ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" /> Though Grievous initially only desired death, he finally relented when Hill brought his barely surviving wives and children before him, on the added condition that he keeps his eyes.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous"/>

Dooku provided [[Blood/Legends|blood]] from the frozen body of Jedi Master [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]] as a means of keeping Grievous's body alive during his transit to Geonosis, where Poggle the Lesser and his [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] implanted his brain and [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] into a [[Duranium/Legends|duranium]] alloy body reminiscent of a [[Krath war droid/Legends|Krath war droid]], complete with [[LX-44 robotic leg/Legends|LX-44 robotic legs]] with magnetized talons,<ref name="ROTS:TVD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and his two [[Electrodriver/Legends|electro-driven]] mechanical [[Limb/Legends|arms]] could split at the dislocating shoulders and create four,<ref name="NEGD" /> like the violent [[Ebranite]] species,<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> each hand having its own dual opposable thumb and articulated finger. His vital organs were housed in a [[Synthskin/Legends|synthskin]] gut-sack impervious to vacuum. The Geonosians would also alter his brain against his wishes, to trim away disturbing memories while enhancing his rage centers, to install a kill-switch, manned by [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] himself, and to enhance his equilibrium, allowing him to better employ his newfound agility. Internal implants were also placed in his eyes to sharpen his vision and to protect them from the vacuum of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="NEGD" /> Grievous had to recover from the crippling change for several [[Standard month/Legends|months]].<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> While the [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorian]]-rich blood of Sifo-Dyas may have played a critical role in maintaining Sheelal's life, Grievous saw it as a personal failure that the transfusion did not also give him a degree of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. To San Hill and his allies, however, the experiment was a phenomenal success. Sheelal had become General Grievous in form as well as spirit.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous"/>

The [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] bionic technology project was funded by San Hill to create a military leader that could counter Dooku's growing political influence in the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Movement]], although he presented the finished General Grievous as a twisted gift to Dooku. Though taken aback by his appearance, Dooku was pleased, and bestowed upon Grievous the title "[[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]]," planning to use him in his efforts to conquer the Republic. He presented him with his first [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], the [[Grievous' first lightsaber/Legends|weapon of Sifo-Dyas]].<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" />

[[File:GrievousTraining-SWI86.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Grievous trains with IG-109.]]
Grievous was disgusted by his new [[Cyborg/Legends|droid]] body and took Dooku's appointment as Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies as an insult. Immediately after he was presented with Dyas' lightsaber, he slaughtered all the MagnaGuards in his presence in a defiant rage, exclaiming that he was not a droid, which Dooku had referred to him as. He also carved a new armorplast death mask that resembled the one he inherited from his father and had it grafted onto his alloy skull, as well as donning an armorweave cape resembling the one he wore duirng the Huk War, which Dooku considered signs of his vanity.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /><ref name="The Eyes of Revolution" />  Grievous, however, would soon come to highly respect both Dooku and Sidious, considering them "necessary" political leadership.<ref name="LOE" />

In particular, Grievous bore a great hatred for the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], tolerating him only because he was vital to the Confederacy's success. Specifically, Grievous was repulsed by Gunray's arrogance and cowardice, and quietly enraged by Gunray's questioning of his leadership,<ref name="ROTS" /> and his defiant tendency to treat Grievous as a typical mindless droid, even after Grievous' demonstrations to the contrary.<ref name="LOE" />

===The Clone Wars===
====The beginning of the war====
{{Quote|More machine than alive, Grievous is—though more dangerous for it.|Jedi Master Yoda|<ref name="LOE" />}}
[[File:UrSemaDuGrievous-SWI86.jpg|thumb|left|235px|Grievous confronted Jedi Master Ur-sema Du in the Geonosian catacombs.]]
Grievous was first let loose in the [[Geonosian catacombs/Legends|Geonosian catacombs]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] where he safeguarded the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] from [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ur-Sema Du]] and [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[Company/Legends|companies]]; he left none alive.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> Although Grievous managed to escape the planet aboard ''[[Soulless One/Legends|Soulless One]]'' without being spotted on the ground, his ship was spotted taking off by [[Clone commando/Legends|Clone commandos]] assigned to [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] shortly after their sniper [[Sev/Legends|Sev]] shot down [[Sun Fac/Legends|Sun Fac's]] own [[Nantex-class territorial defense starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] with his [[DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System/Legends|DC-17m's sniper configuration]]. When squad's technical expert [[RC-1140/Legends|Fixer]] reported that the craft wasn't Geonosian to [[Advisor/Legends|Clone advisor]] [[01/425]], the later was able to confirm the ship's sighting but was unable to find any information on the starfighter or it's pilot which maintained the secrecy of Grievous's existence. Dooku, impressed with the general's performance at Geonosis, trained Grievous in the art of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], which Grievous took to at a rapid pace.<ref name="LOE" />

Learning all the seven classic forms of Jedi arts—including the rarely seen [[Form II/Legends|Makashi]] and [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo]]—Grievous quickly surpassed all the other apprentices of Dooku in terms of individual combat. Despite his obvious prowess, and the time and resources expended to creating him, Dooku still viewed him as second to the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] General [[Sev'rance Tann/Legends|Sev'rance Tann]]. It was only after Tann's [[Battle of Krant|death]] one month after Geonosis that Grievous truly began to come into his own.<ref name="LOE" /><ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns">[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds#Expansion set: Clone Campaigns|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns'']]</ref>

====The General revealed====
{{Quote|Jedi! You are surrounded, your army is decimated. Make peace with the Force now…for this is your final hour. But know that I, General Grievous, am not completely without mercy. I will grant you a warrior's death. Prepare!|Grievous, to Ki-Adi-Mundi and several other Jedi during the Battle of Hypori|audio=MakePeaceWithTheForce-CW20.flac|<ref name="Chapter 20">{{CW|20}}</ref>}}
[[File:GrievousRevealed.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Grievous reveals himself to the Jedi on Hypori.]]
Grievous's first public appearance against the Republic and Jedi Order was at the [[Battle of Hypori/Legends|Battle of Hypori]]<ref name="Chapter 20" /> four months after the Battle of Geonosis.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Grievous led a massive detachment of battle droids to attack the Jedi on [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]], and his tactics resulted in the obliteration of an entire Republic task force. The general cut down Jedi Master [[Daakman Barrek]] as he attempted to request reinforcements from the Jedi [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who were simultaneously [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|fighting]] on [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]]. With six other Jedi—[[Tarr Seirr]], [[Sha'a Gi]], [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], [[K'Kruhk]], and [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] members [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] and [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]]—trapped in the remains of a downed [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class transport]], Grievous ordered his [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droid]] troops to stand down, effectively surrounding the Jedi. The general addressed the trapped Jedi, stating that he would grant them a "warrior's death" and lying in wait for them to move. Once [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] Gi ran screaming into the unprotected open, Grievous jumped on and killed him. The general then perched himself on the top of the transport and hung from this point, surveying the five remaining Jedi Knights before landing below and engaging them in combat, unleashing vicious dual-lightsaber attacks on his adversaries.<ref name="Chapter 20" />

Grievous first targeted Mundi, advancing toward his opponent with the other Jedi in pursuit. Although Mundi evaded the general's powerful downward slash and released a [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force-push]] at him, Grievous evaded the blast and jumped onto a nearby wall, propelling himself at the Knights and blasting them aside upon impact. Grievous cut down the attacking K'Kruhk down, slashed through the rubble thrown at him by Ti, picked up the advancing Seirr by the head with one of his mechanical feet and slammed him to the ground face first, and grabbed Secura as well, throwing both Seirr and Secura up against the top of the transport's remains above. Grievous then dueled both Masters Mundi and Ti at once. He managed to counter their attacks and eventually kicked Mundi against a nearby pile of rubble. Unfazed, the cyborg general advanced at Ti. Shaak Ti desperately tried to defend herself but was unable to escape his onslaught. Grievous quickly overwhelmed her, knocking her lightsaber out of her hand and kicked her hard against a pile of debris. A recovered Mundi attempted to retrieve his lightsaber with the Force, only to have Grievous trap the weapon beneath one of his clawed feet and pick it up himself. With Grievous in possession of three lightsabers (one in each hand and the third he wielded using his left foot), Mundi stole one of the lightsabers secured at his waist, and Grievous jumped at Mundi, lightsabers blazing.<ref name="Chapter 20" />

[[File:Grievous-Attacks-Ki-Adi-Mundi-And-Shaak-Ti.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Grievous engaged Ki-Adi Mundi and Shaak Ti.]]
As Grievous fought Mundi, an [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commando]] clone trooper squad led by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Fordo]] arrived in an [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i gunship]] to rescue the Jedi. While several clones followed the life signs of the surviving Jedi, Fordo led other troopers to rescue Mundi just as Grievous was preparing to kill the disarmed Jedi Master. The ARC troopers opened fire on Grievous, who evaded the blasts, running across the roof of the compound. Grievous then landed on the ground, cutting through several troopers. Fordo brought in the LAAT/i [[Gunship/Legends|gunship]], and Grievous quickly ran from the craft's laser fire and rockets. While Mundi and the ARC troopers escaped with Secura and Ti under treatment to recover from the devastating battle, Grievous stole the fallen K'Kruhk's lightsaber and added it to his collection of ''trophies'' around his waist. Grievous watched as the Republic gunship fled from Hypori, taunting the Jedi and stating that they had "only prolonged the inevitable."<ref name="Chapter 21">{{CW|21}}</ref>

After that battle, Grievous was given a grueling monogram from Jedi Master [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]: the Butcher of Hypori.<ref name="Lightsaber Duels">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels]]''</ref>

[[File:GrievousNadiem.jpg|right|thumb|200px|Grievous realizes that his army has been defeated.]]
Five months after the Battle of Geonosis, Grievous led an assault on the Outer Rim planet of [[Nadiem/Legends|Nadiem]]. His armies were able to secure a strong foothold on the world before a Republic detachment, led by [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] and [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]], arrived to stop his advance. Grievous ordered the movements of the Separatist army from a base far from the front, and though Tiin and a Republic fleet defeated his air support, Grievous made significant gains. Grievous sent his forward armies through a strategic canyon to attack the Republic's main army, where they were ambushed by clone troopers and [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]], Unduli's Padawan. Though the droids appeared to have defeated the clones, they were only pretending to be dead, and attacked the army from behind when it engaged Unduli's forces at the other end of the canyon.<ref name="Hide in Plain Sight">{{CWACite|2|Hide in Plain Sight}}</ref> Grievous's forces were outmaneuvered and destroyed, leaving Grievous to abandon the battle in his personal starfighter. The Jedi Master [[B'dard Tone]] and his apprentice attempted to stop Grievous, but Tone was wounded and his apprentice was killed.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

Not long after this, Count Dooku tested Grievous by [[Mission to Trenchant space station|pitting]] him against fellow Separatist [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] and [[Durge/Legends|Durge]] aboard the Count's [[Space Station Trenchant/Legends|Trenchant space station]]. After Durge and Ventress had been lured onto the station, Grievous snuck up on Durge, shocking him from behind with an [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]] and throwing him across the room through the various trophies there.<ref name="Rogue's Gallery">{{CWACite|3|Rogue's Gallery}}</ref>

[[File:Durgegrievous.jpg|left|thumb|200px|Grievous cuts through Durge on Trenchant space station.]]
When Ventress jumped onto a dragon hanging from the ceiling and attempted to find Grievous, he instead snuck up on her and knocked her off her perch with the blunt end of his staff. Although Durge caught the falling Ventress, Grievous soon confronted the pair face-to-face. The general threw Ventress into a glass case and was caught around the neck by one of Durge's flails. Ventress then attacked Grievous from behind as he removed the flail, slashing at the cyborg with her [[Interlocking hilt|paired lightsabers]], and Durge contributed to the fight, punching Grievous and slamming him through a statue of Count Dooku. As Durge and Ventress advanced, Grievous activated two of his lightsabers, cutting into Durge and beheading the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]. Grievous saber locked with Ventress and was slammed into a containment case by the [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolyte]]. Despite his injuries, Grievous grabbed Ventress in a choke, responding to her probes about his identity by stating that he was "the future." With that, Grievous choked Ventress unconscious.<ref name="Rogue's Gallery" />

The cyborg general brought Ventress's inert body to a meeting with Count Dooku, questioning if he could jettison both bodies. Dooku refused the request and ordered them to be put in bacta tanks, stating that they had proven themselves and citing their loyalty. However, Grievous had successfully humiliated both Separatist commanders, showing Dooku his worthiness of holding the position of Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies.<ref name="Rogue's Gallery" /> The General's skill at fighting Jedi prompted Republic [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] to nickname him "The Knight Slayer."<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" /> As Supreme Commander, Grievous normally traveled with a cadre of IG-100 MagnaGuards, who wielded dangerous electrostaffs made from lightsaber-resistant [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]] alloy.<ref name="ROTS" /> Grievous quickly became the face of the Confederacy, and was feared by countless citizens loyal to the Republic.<ref name="LOE" /> His role as Supreme Commander led to the Republic's clone troopers nicknaming him the "head clanker."<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence">{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

Count Dooku dispatched Grievous to the icy world of [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]] to investigate the disappearance of a battle droid army, which had vanished alongside the [[313th Legion]], the Republic [[Company/Legends|unit]] that it had been [[Battle of Ando Prime|battling]]. The cyborg general and his droid squad of twelve were initially unable to locate the unit and reported back to the Separatist Head of State, who ordered Grievous to continue searching, as a loss of this magnitude was unaffordable for the Separatists. As the general continued to search for the vanished droid army, he and his squad were ambushed by the Republic [[Company/Legends|unit]] [[Excelsior Company]], which was also there to investigate the disappearance of the Republic forces. Led by [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Vargus]], the clone trooper detachment eliminated Grievous's droids and forced the cyborg to flee.<ref name="The Lost Legion">''[[The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny: The Lost Legion]]''</ref>

====The ''Malevolence''====
{{Quote|Do not compound your failure this day by allowing our prized warship to fall.''"<br />"''My lord, they will never capture me or this ship.|Count Dooku and Grievous|<ref name="Destroy Malevolence">{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}</ref>}}
[[File:Battle_of_Abregado.jpg|thumb|right|230px|The ''Malevolence'', commanded by Grievous, ravages Plo Koon's fleet in the Abregado system.]]
As the war continued, Grievous took the [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser]] [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] as his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]]. The [[Warship/Legends|warship]] possessed two [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]] that were capable of disabling entire fleets, leaving them vulnerable to the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] fire. Under the general's command, the ''Malevolence'' began executing attacks on Republic fleets that left no survivors.<ref name="Rising Malevolence">{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}</ref> After [[Battle of the Phu system/Legends|eradicating]] a Republic task force in the [[Phu system/Legends|Phu system]],<ref name="Shakedown">''[[The Clone Wars: Shakedown]]''</ref> Grievous and the ''Malevolence'' were stationed in the [[Abregado system/Legends|Abregado system]] with Count Dooku, who had arrived aboard the warship to supervise Grievous's progress. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] led a task force to find and destroy the Separatist [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], and arrived in the system to engage the warship. Before the Jedi could get in firing range, Grievous ordered the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} battle droid crew to fire an ion blast at the Republic fleet. After the Star Destroyers' [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] were disabled, the ''Malevolence'' opened fire and eradicated the fleet, scattering a debris field in the system from the wreckage of the Republic [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]].<ref name="Rising Malevolence" />

While Grievous deemed the destruction of the Republic fleet a successful test, Dooku dispatched a [[Droch-class boarding ship/Legends|''Droch''-class craft]]—nicknamed a "pod hunter" for its purposes—with [[Rocket battle droid/Legends|rocket battle droids]] aboard to locate and eliminate the Republic's [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. During the craft's hunt for life pods, however, the ''Malevolence'' lost contact with the pod hunter, and Grievous mused that perhaps some survivors were putting up a fight. As the ''Malevolence'' activated its scanners, the battle droid crew picked up a signal from a non-Separatist droid, and Grievous immediately ordered his warship to assume attack position. The battle droids then picked up the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] ''Twilight''—carrying Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano, who had rescued Plo Koon and the survivors of the battle—attempting to escape from the debris field. Dooku reminded his general that he did not want any witnesses, and Grievous ordered the ion cannon to be charged and fired. However, the ''Twilight'' evaded the ion blast by jumping to hyperspace, taking the knowledge of the warship's weapons to the Republic. Considering the battle a defeat because of this, Dooku's trust in Grievous was shaken, and the Sith Lord left to discuss plans with his master, Darth Sidious.<ref name="Rising Malevolence" />

With Count Dooku watching his progress via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]], Grievous [[Battle of the Ryndellia system/Legends|intercepted]] and eradicated a Republic medical convoy in the [[Ryndellia system/Legends|Ryndellia system]]. Dooku had recently met with Darth Sidious and had learned of the [[Kaliida Shoals Medical Center/Legends|Kaliida Shoals Medical Center]], the Republic's secret [[Medcenter/Legends|medical facility]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] that was treating over 60,000 wounded clones. Dooku assigned the medical center as the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} new target, seeking to exploit the weakness that the Jedi displayed in their care for their clone troopers. This assignment boosted Grievous's confidence, as it showed that the Count had not completely lost his faith in him since his recent failure at Abregado. As the remaining [[Pelta-class frigate/Legends|Republic frigate]] deployed several escape pods, Grievous ordered the pods to be targeted, stating that he had "a reputation to uphold." To get to the medical station, the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]] was forced to calculate a complex hyperspace course around the [[Kaliida Nebula/Legends|Kaliida Nebula]], which was near the medcenter. Grievous was frustrated with the setback, as he wanted to maximize his casualties and did not want too many wounded clones to be given the chance to evacuate the station before his arrival.<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence" />

[[File:Grievous_SOM.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous confers with Count Dooku aboard the ''Malevolence''.]]
''En route'' to Kaliida Shoals, Grievous received word from Count Dooku that the Republic had launched a small strike force under the command of Anakin Skywalker to [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula/Legends|intercept]] the warship. The Sith Lord advised his general not to underestimate the Jedi, but Grievous maintained that it would be Skywalker who would underestimate the Separatist ship. Skywalker's [[Shadow Squadron/Legends|starfighter squadron]] took a [[Balmorra Run/Legends|shortcut]] through the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]], and Grievous arrived shortly thereafter. As the Jedi and his fighters approached, Grievous launched Vulture droids from the ''Malevolence'' to attack the Republic squadron while the warship itself targeted the medical transports attempting to escape from the medical center. The superweapon made haste with disabling the frigates before tearing them apart with [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire. Grievous ordered the ion cannon to be charged and targeted at the Republic squadron, despite the fact that his own Vulture droid starfighters would be caught in the blast. The battle droids complied, decimating Skywalker's fighters.<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence" />

As the Jedi closed in on the warship with his remaining forces, Grievous targeted the Kaliida Shoals Medcenter, seeking to destroy the medical facility before attending to Skywalker. However, the Republic squadron attacked the ion cannon, and once the ''Malevolence'' attempted to fire its deadly weapon at the medcenter, the cannon exploded, triggering a chain reaction that rocked and greatly damaged the ship. With the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} primary weapons disabled, Grievous ordered a full retreat to Separatist space. General Obi-Wan Kenobi then arrived in the system with a fleet of three ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers and began to attack Grievous's ravaged flagship.<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence" /> As the ''Malevolence'' fled under increasing fire from the Republic cruisers, Dooku contacted Grievous and informed the general that [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of the Republic had been tricked into traveling to the nebula; with her as a hostage, Grievous would be able to safely escape. At first, the general believed that such a tactic was unnecessary, but eventually complied with the Sith Lord's plan. Amidala's [[H-type Nubian yacht/Legends|ship]] arrived out of hyperspace just off the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} bow, and Grievous ordered the [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]] to be captured with the warship's [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]].<ref name="Destroy Malevolence" />

After Senator Amidala had been pulled into the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} main hangar via the tractor beam, the Republic Star Destroyers ceased their fire. Grievous ordered a repair crew to be brought up to the warship's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] and proceeded to the landing bay to apprehend his hostage. However, Amidala had overloaded her ship's engines before hiding elsewhere in the hangar. After taking his warship's [[Rail jet/Legends|rail jet]] to the hangar, Grievous entered Amidala's ship with two B1 battle droids and discovered her exploit. Pushing the battle droids out of the way, Grievous headed for the exit, but the ship exploded before he could run for safety. The general survived the explosion and cleared himself out of the rubble. Leading the battle droids' search for the stowaway Senator through the warship's hallways, Grievous soon received word from his ship's droid crew that the hyperdrive would require less time than originally believed to repair. Ordering his troops to continue the search for the Senator, the general left to inform Count Dooku of this new development. On the bridge, Grievous learned that there had been an unauthorized communication inside the ship, but was angered when he discovered that the battle droids had not caught it in time to intercept it. The general ordered his crew to monitor all internal communications to locate the Senator.<ref name="Destroy Malevolence" />

[[File:Kenobi_vs_Grievous_Malevolence.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous and Kenobi duel on the rail jets aboard the ''Malevolence''.]]
Taking the ''Twilight'' to the warship, Skywalker and Kenobi arrived aboard the ''Malevolence'' and rendezvoused with Amidala at the rail jet junction. Kenobi planned to sabotage the warship's hyperdrive, while Skywalker and Amidala would meet him back at the ''Twilight''. However, Grievous intercepted their [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] transmission, and took a squad of battle droids with him to ambush Kenobi. After Kenobi arrived in the hyperdrive room, Grievous's deployed battle droids surrounded the Jedi Master, and the cyborg himself jumped down from a higher level to confront him. Grievous ordered the droids to kill Kenobi, but the Jedi defeated the majority of the droids before using a remaining [[Droideka/Legends|droideka's]] deflector shield as protection from Grievous's oncoming [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] fire. Kenobi then Force-pushed the droid toward Grievous. As the Separatist general picked up the droideka and hurtled it aside, Kenobi escaped. Grievous took his frustration out on a battle droid who commented on Kenobi's abilities, ordering his troops to guard the hyperdrive before departing to deal with Kenobi himself.<ref name="Destroy Malevolence" />

Grievous found Kenobi aboard a rail jet car and saberlocked with him, pursing Kenobi after he broke the bladelock. The cyborg knocked Kenobi on his back, but as Grievous prepared to kill the Jedi, Kenobi jumped onto another railjet, saluting the general as he left. Grievous boarded the ''[[Soulless One/Legends|Soulless One]]'' and took a squadron of Vulture droids to attack the fleeing Jedi and Senator, who were returning to the Republic fleet in the ''Twilight''. During the [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]], a B1 battle droid contacted Grievous and informed him that the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} hyperdrive was almost completely repaired. The general ordered the ''Malevolence'' to retreat to hyperspace, arranging to meet his warship at a [[Sector Four Confederacy base/Legends|Separatist base]] in [[Sector Four (Confederacy)/Legends|Sector Four]]. However, Skywalker had sabotaged the warship's navicomputer before escaping. As the ''Malevolence'' headed toward the nearby [[Dead Moon of Antar/Legends|Dead Moon of Antar]], Grievous ordered the warship's crew to reset the navicomputer. Dooku contacted Grievous, stating that the general and his warship were being awaited at the rendezvous point. Manually cutting off the transmission, Grievous engaged his fighter's hyperdrive and retreated shortly before the ''Malevolence'' crashed into the moon.<ref name="Destroy Malevolence" />

====Victories over the Republic====
{{Quote|You are too slow and too late, assassin. More Republic forces have arrived to reinforce the Jedi—and I have already given the order to exit the system. I'm afraid you are on your own.''"<br />"''Enjoy your retreat, General. It seems to be what you do best.|Grievous and Asajj Ventress, during the battle at Kadavo|<ref name="Escape from Kadavo">[[The Clone Wars 6|''The Clone Wars'' 6]]</ref>}}
As the war progressed, Grievous led Separatists forces to [[Battle of Anoth (Clone Wars)|fight]] on the planet [[Anoth/Legends|Anoth]] and [[Battle of Bakura (Clone Wars)|battle]] on the planet [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]], engaging Jedi Knights Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi both times. The general also had his battle droid forces on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] [[Battle of Ord Mantell (Clone Wars)|raze]] an entire civilian township to divert Republic troops and allow himself to escape. Grievous eventually captured crucial [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] routes running to [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], and [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]], totaling six Separatist victories that month. The capture of the lanes jeopardized the supplies of [[Tibanna/Legends|tibanna gas]] and Kessel [[Spice/Legends|spice]], leading to civilian suffering, and also prevented the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] from engaging in an "ages-old ritual."<ref name="Wild Space">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref>

Grievous returned to the flamegrass plains of Tovarskl with his droid army to complete what he had begun during the Huk War and [[Battle of Tovarskl|slaughtered]] the Yam'rii population to a crisp. Grievous engaged the [[Eirrauc]] Jedi Master [[Puroth]] and the [[Vuvrian]] Jedi Master [[Nystammall]], and Puroth became one of his greatest difficulties before he de-[[Dismemberment/Legends|limbed]] and killed both masters.<ref name="The Story of General Grievous" />

====Battle of Bothawui====
{{Quote|Move our ships through the asteroid field to engage them.''"<br />"Through'' the field, sir?''"<br />"''If we attack from above, they will have the advantage. So we will go through the rocks.|Grievous and his OOM command battle droid|<ref name="Downfall of a Droid">{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}</ref>}}
[[File:Grievous_Battle_of_Bothawui.png|thumb|left|230px|Grievous leads a Separatist fleet during the Battle of Bothawui.]]
Grievous then planned to capture [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], the strategical world of the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] that was critical to [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]]. When the Jedi Council learned of the general's plan, Anakin Skywalker and his Padawan learner, [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], were dispatched with a newly-christened [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] to stop the cyborg. Grievous cut the Jedi out of their hyperlanes and [[Battle of Bothawui/Legends|engaged]] the Jedi three times in open space before Skywalker and his fleet escaped and took a direct course to Bothawui.<ref name="Wild Space" />

Grievous halted his pursuit of Skywalker's fleet to coordinate attacks on Republic forces on separate fronts. Picking up two more [[Munificent-class star frigate/Legends|''Munificent''-class star frigates]], Grievous then [[Fall of Falleen|overwhelmed]] a Republic [[Battle group/Legends|battle group]] stationed at the planet [[Falleen (planet)/Legends|Falleen]].<ref name="Wild Space" /> With the added aid of Count Dooku and Asajj Ventress themselves, Grievous was able to capture the planet<ref name="The Fall of Falleen">''[[The Clone Wars: The Fall of Falleen]]''</ref> and headed to invade Bothawui. Grievous's fleet of six ''Munificent''-class [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] arrived out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] in front of [[Golm|Bothawui Prime's]] [[Golm asteroid belt|asteroid belt]], and at the general's order, the [[Starship/Legends|ships]] of the fleet directed all power to their forward shields and proceeded through the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]]. As soon as it emerged from the [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belt]], Grievous's fleet [[Battle of Bothawui/Legends|attacked]] Skywalker's three [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]]. However, a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of Republic [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE walkers]] had been deployed to the asteroids and opened fire on the fleet from behind, giving Grievous a nasty surprise.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid" />

Frustrated with the failed attack, Grievous left an [[Unidentified OOM command battle droid (Bothawui)/Legends|OOM battle droid]] in command of the fleet and fled in ''Soulless One''. His [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was pursued by Skywalker himself in [[Anakin Skywalker's Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|his Delta-7B fighter]], but thanks in part to flying debris that damaged Skywalker's fighter, Grievous was able to jump to hyperspace and retreat. Following the defeat at Bothawui, the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Scavenger/Legends|scavenger]] [[Gha Nachkt/Legends|Gha Nachkt]] contacted Grievous, informing the general that he had salvaged [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], Skywalker's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]], from the Bothawui asteroid belt. Grievous agreed to "buy" the droid from the scavenger, but threatened Nachkt when he attempted to raise the arranged price for the droid.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid" />

====Encounter on Skytop Station====
{{Quote|Sorry to interrupt your playtime, ''grumpy'', but wouldn't you prefer a ''challenge?<br />"''That wouldn't be you!|Ahsoka Tano and Grievous, after the latter attempts to kill the unconscious Rex|audio=InteruptPlaytime-DotD.flac|<ref name="Duel of the Droids">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ahsoka_vs_Grievous.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Grievous duels Ahsoka Tano aboard Skytop Station.]]
Grievous's [[Spy/Legends|spy]] droid, [[R3-S6/Legends|R3-S6]]—who had been assigned to Skywalker as his replacement astromech—soon activated the [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] of the Jedi's fighter during a [[Mission to suspected Confederate space/Legends|mission]] to scout ahead for enemy activity. Grievous arrived with two frigates to ambush the Jedi, and [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Vulture droids]] were launched from the Separatist fleet to attack Skywalker. However, Tano arrived with Skywalker's personal ship, the [[Twilight/Legends|''Twilight'']], to rescue her Master, causing Grievous to smack a nearby [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] out of frustration.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid" /> Grievous then went to the Separatist [[Listening post/Legends|listening post]] [[Skytop Station/Legends|Skytop Station]], located over [[Ruusan 2/Legends|one]] of the [[Moon/Legends|moons]] of [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]], to rendezvous with Nachkt and retrieve the droid. Once the scavenger had arrived with R2-D2 at the [[Space station/Legends|space station]], Grievous ordered Nachkt to take the droid apart and access his [[Memory bank/Legends|memory banks]]. The preceding investigation revealed that R2-D2's mission memory had never been erased, and when Nachkt demanded a higher pay, Grievous replied by impaling the Trandoshan in the back with his lightsaber. The general then learned from his spy, R3-S6, that the Jedi had arrived aboard his station to [[Raid on Skytop Station/Legends|destroy]] it, and ordered his IG-100 MagnaGuards to guard R2-D2. Shortly before revealing himself to Tano and a squad of clone troopers, Grievous ordered the astromech droid to be taken to ''Soulless One''.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" />

Confronting Tano and her clone squad, Grievous batted the Padawan aside before attacking and killing all but two of the [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]]. As the general prepared to kill [[Clone Captain/Legends|Clone Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|CT-7567]], Tano regained consciousness and blocked his lightsaber blow. Grievous was doubtful that Tano would provide a challenge for him, but engaged the Padawan in combat before following her and R3-S6 into a storage room. The two engaged in a game of cat and mouse as Grievous chased and engaged Tano, and with the general occupied, CT-7567 and [[Denal/Legends|the other clone]] were able to plant explosives in the station's [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]] room. When R3-S6 received word that Skywalker had arrived to retrieve his R2 unit and was planning to rendezvous with the rest of his men in the landing bay, the general ordered his spy droid to prevent the Jedi and clones from escaping. Hanging from the ceiling, Grievous found Tano and clamped a metal hand around the Padawan's throat, examining her fallen lightsaber with his free hand.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" />

Despite Tano's claims that her Master would destroy Skytop Station, Grievous believed otherwise. However, Tano's beliefs proved true when the Republic squad detonated the explosives in the reactor room, crippling the listening post's [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] systems. As the station shook from the impact, Tano managed to use her lightsaber to sever the hand clamped around her throat. Although Grievous attempted to slash her with one of his lightsabers, Tano retrieved her weapon and escaped through an air duct. While Skytop Station plummeted from the sky, Grievous escaped in ''Soulless One'' empty-handed, lacking the Republic droid or another stolen Jedi lightsaber to add to his collection.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" />

At some point during the war, Darth Sidious gave Grievous a set of Republic code keys, giving the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] the opportunity to [[Battle of JanFathal|take control]] of the planet [[JanFathal]] in the [[Fath system]].<ref name="No Prisoners">''[[The Clone Wars: No Prisoners]]''</ref> Grievous also launched an [[Battle of Kothlis (Clone Wars)|assault]] on the planet [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]], a fact which the Republic managed to learn. The Republic sent a fleet to confront Grievous, and was able to drive him away.<ref name="Gambit: Stealth">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Stealth]]''</ref> During a [[Battle of Nexus Ortai|battle]] at [[Nexus Ortai/Legends|Nexus Ortai]] against Republic forces, Grievous arrived with a fleet of ''Munificent''-class frigates and a single [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]] to reinforce the Separatist fleet over the planet, forcing the Republic out of the [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="Shipyards of Doom">''[[The Clone Wars: Shipyards of Doom]]''</ref>

====Proving his competence====
{{Quote|You might have been a proud warrior once, but now you are just a pawn in Dooku's game!''"<br />"''I wield ''great'' power, Jedi ''fool!''"<br />"That power will only consume you.|Kit Fisto and Grievous during their duel|<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous|d=y}}</ref>}}
[[File:Vebb_Grievous_Fisto.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Grievous activates two more of his lightsabers during combat with the Jedi.]]
Later in the war, Grievous targeted the Republic's cloning facilities on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], intending to stop the production of clone troopers for good. To prevent the Republic from learning of the impending invasion, Grievous sent droid squads to seize all Republic outposts in the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] and hot-wire the stations' "all-clear" signals.<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref> Despite her rivalries with Grievous,<ref name="Escape from Kadavo" /><ref name="TCWTVG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> Asajj Ventress made the necessary preparations on Kamino for the general's invasion. A [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commando]] squad [[Defense of Rishi Station/Legends|overran]] a [[Rishi Station/Legends|Republic outpost]] on [[Rishi moon|the moon]] of [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]], and after the droids reported their success to Grievous, Ventress contacted the general with the news that all the preparations on Kamino were in order. As the Separatist fleet approached the [[Kamino system/Legends|Kamino system]], Grievous learned that the droid commandos on the moon had stopped responding. Seeking to ensure that the base did not alert the Jedi of his approaching fleet, the general ordered reinforcements to be sent to the station. However, a squad of clone troopers put up a fight and destroyed the base, alerting the Republic to Grievous's presence in the system. The Republic fleet arrived over the moon and opened fire at the Separatist cruisers, and with his fleet outgunned, Grievous and his ships fled the system.<ref name="Rookies" /> The [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] later issued a "dead or alive" warrant on the cyborg general.<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" />

During the war, Grievous held a [[Grievous's castle/Legends|castle]] on the [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon]] of the planet [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek]],<ref name="Lair of Grievous Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode010.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lair of Grievous}}</ref> where he housed his pet [[Roggwart/Legends|roggwart]], [[Gor/Legends|Gor]]<ref name="Lair of Grievous">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref>—a fearsome creature whom Grievous "doted on"<ref name="OEG:S1">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]''</ref>—in addition to spare parts and trophies from the Jedi he had murdered. [[EV-A4-D/Legends|EV-A4-D]], his repair droid, also resided in the general's lair.<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" /> While returning to his castle in ''Soulless One'', Grievous dreamed of his past as a Kaleesh warlord and his transformation into a cyborg.<ref name="The Dreams of General Grievous">"[[The Clone Wars: The Dreams of General Grievous]]"</ref> However, when he entered his stronghold, he discovered that his MagnaGuard bodyguards had been shut down. The general was soon confronted by the Jedi [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] and [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]] with a squad of clone troopers. Drawing two of his lightsabers, Grievous engaged the two Jedi in lightsaber combat before splitting his arms and activating two more of his stolen Jedi weapons. The clones fired [[Grappling hook/Legends|grappling hooks]] at the cyborg's legs, and Fisto severed the general's limbs below the cables.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> Although he felt no pain,<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" /> the loss of his legs put Grievous at a disadvantage in agility.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

The general jumped up to hold a beam on the roof, but the clones quickly pulled him back down to the ground. Attempting to crawl away, Grievous was confronted by Vebb, and the general's lightsaber spun out of his hand. Grievous again jumped up to hang from the roof, but this time succeeded in severing the cables attached to his legs. Batting a dead clone against Fisto, the general then threw the trooper onto Vebb before sustaining a blaster shot to his face and fleeing. The Jedi and clones gave pursuit, but Grievous attacked two troopers and entered the sanctuary of his hidden command center. Splitting his arms again, the cyborg opened the door to the center by touching its panels in a certain sequence. Learning from [[EV-A4-D/Legends|EV-A4-D]] that his droid bodyguards had been remotely deactivated for recharge, Grievous activated his MagnaGuards and ordered them to lock down the perimeter. Watching the Jedi and remaining clones retreat via a [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid/Legends|droid holocam]], Grievous sealed off all the exits from his castle and trapped the squad inside his lair. The general conferred with the Jedi via holotransmission before severing the connection and opening up a molten incinerator pit, dropping one of the clones into its depths. As Grievous continued to watch the Jedi's progress, Fisto drove his lightsaber into the holocam. Undaunted, the general told Gor it was "time to entertain their guests" and released him to confront the Jedi before EV-A4-D began repairs on the cyborg.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

After his repairs had been completed, Grievous was temporarily confined to his chair to allow his new legs to set in.<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" /> Checking on Gor's progress with the Jedi, Grievous discovered that Gor had been killed and that the Jedi had escaped. Angered with the loss of his roggwart<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> and finding it another "wrong that the Jedi Order would pay dearly for,"<ref name="OEG:S1" /> Grievous soon discovered from Dooku that it was the Sith Lord himself who had deactivated his MagnaGuards and let the Jedi into his lair in order to reassess the cyborg general in light of his recent failures at the Jedi's hands. Cutting off the transmission, Grievous stated that he would "play the Count's little game," and resolved to hunt down the Jedi for sport. Although EV-A4-D stated that he required rest in light of his recent repairs, Grievous was determined to find and kill the Jedi. The general left his command center with several MagnaGuards, but was soon alerted by EV-A4-D that the Jedi were about to enter the hidden room. Grievous immediately turned around to confront the Jedi, and while Fisto escaped into the command center, Vebb was determined to fight Grievous and remained outside as EV-A4-D shut the door. Vebb cut his way through Grievous's bodyguards and entered into lightsaber combat with the cyborg. As the two opponents blade-locked, Grievous took out a blaster with one of his free arms and shot the Jedi, taking the fallen Vebb's lightsaber for his own collection.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

[[File:FistovsGrievous.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous duels Fisto on the castle's outer platform with a severed hand.]]
Knowing that Fisto was watching from inside the control room, Grievous stated that he was his next target, and pursued the Jedi out to the castle's outer platform. Climbing onto the platform from below, Grievous appeared to Fisto and engaged the Jedi Master in combat. Fisto used the fog to his advantage and deactivated his lightsaber to sneak up on the cyborg. Spinning his four lightsabers in defense, Grievous found himself confronted by Fisto from behind, and the two duelists continued their fight. As Grievous swung a lightsaber at the Jedi,<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> Fisto severed the hand of the cyborg that held Vebb's lightsaber and reclaimed it.<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" /> Grievous was forced to give ground, but Fisto managed to land a blow on the cyborg and Force-pushed him off-balance. The general quickly got back up and continued the duel with renewed vigor. Suddenly, three of the cyborg's MagnaGuards appeared and attacked the Jedi. With Fisto surrounded and outnumbered, Grievous demanded his surrender. However, Fisto's [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B fighter]] appeared, piloted by Fisto's [[R6-H5/Legends|astromech droid]]. Before Grievous or his MagnaGuards could stop him, Fisto escaped.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

Returning to his castle and entering the stronghold's sanctum overlook chamber,<ref name="Lair of Grievous Decoded" /> Grievous conferred with Dooku via holotransmission and learned that victory over the clones and the young Jedi, Vebb, had been expected. At first, Dooku believed that Grievous had also bested the Jedi Master Fisto and was pleased with this accomplishment. However, Dooku was disappointed when he learned that Fisto had escaped, stating that there was "room for improvement" before severing the connection and leaving Grievous alone with his frustration.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> Grievous eventually had EV-A4-D rebuilt to continue his service as a doctor and adviser.<ref name="Prelude to Point Rain">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20091103fd/index.html|text=Fan Days Script: A Prelude to "Point Rain"}}</ref>

====Stands against the Jedi====
{{Quote|Your plans have come to ruination, Jedi!''"<br />"''I hear a lot of talking, General, but in the final accounting, what does all the talk get you? A futile quest for power, a mutilated body? Your place is Dooku's ''errand boy!''"<br />"I'm no errand boy. And I'm not in this war for Dooku's politics. I am the leader of the most powerful droid army the galaxy has ever seen!''"<br />"''An army with no loyalty, no spirit, just ''programming''. What have you to show for all your power? What have you to ''gain?''"<br />"The future. A future where there are ''no Jedi!''<nowiki></nowiki>|Grievous and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref>}}
[[File:Grievous-Intrigue-old-thumbnail.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous engaging Kenobi in combat.]]
Later in the war, Grievous initiated an [[First Battle of Felucia/Legends|assault]] on the planet [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]].<ref name="DB Felucia">{{DB|location|felucia|Felucia}}</ref> The Separatists were eventually able to defeat the Jedi-led Republic forces there through sheer numbers, forcing the Republic to pull out from the world.<ref name="Holocron Heist">{{TCW|Holocron Heist}}</ref> Later, Grievous would personally venture to Felucia, where he [[Duel on Felucia|engaged Kenobi in a lightsaber duel]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Accompanied by EV-A4-D, Grievous also took Separatist forces to [[Battle of Dorin|attack]] the planet [[Dorin/Legends|Dorin]], home to the Republic-allied [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dors]], in order to distract the Jedi from raiding Geonosis, where several secret Separatist droid foundries were in operation. While the general was taking pleasure in decimating the "Republic filth" from his command ship, EV-A4-D notified him of an incoming top-level transmission from Asajj Ventress. Grievous initially refused to take the transmission, but agreed to receive it when his medical droid stated that the Dark Acolyte could be reporting information from Count Dooku. The cyborg conferred with Ventress, who verbally toyed with him before eventually informing Grievous that a large Republic fleet under the command of Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano had left [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to reinforce Dorin. Grievous was confident in his abilities to defeat the Jedi, though Ventress mockingly expressed her beliefs for the contrary. Grievous recalled his forces and prepared his fighters in preparation for Skywalker's arrival,<ref name="Prelude to Point Rain" /> but he was ultimately unable to defeat the Jedi.<ref name="Landing at Point Rain">{{TCW|Landing at Point Rain}}</ref>

Though the Republic was desperate to capture Grievous, they were unable to predict where he would strike next. In one battle, the General's [[Grievous's Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|Separatist destroyer]] [[Capture of Eeth Koth/Legends|attacked]] a ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer commanded by the Jedi [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]]. Koth ordered his clone troopers to abandon the ship while he stayed behind to confront the cyborg on the ship's bridge. Grievous boarded the Star Destroyer and plowed through the clone troopers until he reached the bridge. Grievous cut his way through the sealed door, and then stood back, while several of his [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|commando droids]] assaulted the bridge. However, they were defeated, prompting Grievous to call in his MagnaGuards, who surrounded Koth. Grievous mocked Koth, who in turn called him a coward and a murderer. The two dueled, with Koth using the Force to gain a brief advantage. However, he was then subdued by a MagnaGuard, and taken hostage. Grievous proudly broadcast his victory over Koth directly to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. In his message, he proudly proclaimed that he had defeated Koth, and swore that he lived to kill the Jedi as he [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] Koth, promising that the Jedi Master's death would be slow, much to the horror of the Jedi watching.<ref name="Intrigue" />

Unnoticed to Grievous, Koth was able to use a hand signal as he was being tortured, indicating that the general was in the [[Saleucami system/Legends|Saleucami system]]. The Republic sent a rescue mission led by Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, and [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] in hopes of [[Battle of Saleucami/Legends|freeing Koth and defeating Grievous]]. When the Republic ships arrived at [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]], Kenobi broadcast a message to Grievous, knowing that it would entice the cyborg to attempt to board the Republic vessel in hopes of personally killing the Jedi Master. With Grievous distracted, Skywalker and Gallia were able to board Grievous's ship, and make their way to the bridge, where Koth was being held. Meanwhile, Grievous boarded the Republic vessel, and engaged Kenobi in combat. Grievous revealed to him that he was aware that Skywalker was on board his vessel.<ref name="Intrigue" />

[[File:Grievous vs. Kenobi Saleucami.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Grievous attempt to flee from Kenobi.]]
Gallia and Skywalker managed to find Koth, but were then ambushed by a group of BX-series commandos. Despite being outnumbered, the duo were able to defeat the commando droids and [[TV-94/Legends|TV-94]], and rescue Eeth Koth. Back on the Republic vessel, Grievous fled from Kenobi after being unable to defeat the Jedi Master. While running back to his own ship, he ordered his droids to fire on the engines of the Republic vessel docked to his [[Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|''Recusant''-class light destroyer]]. If all went as planned, he would return to his ship just before the Republic ship exploded, killing Kenobi and trapping the other Jedi on board the Separatist vessel. Though Grievous was able to escape, Kenobi was saved from the vacuum of space by Gallia. Skywalker was able to make it back to the Jedi's shuttle with Koth, and then land it in the ''Recusant''{{'s}} hangar, enabling the Jedi to escape.<ref name="Intrigue" />

Grievous in turn climbed into a [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]], taking it to Saleucami's surface. The Jedi were informed of this by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], and Kenobi decided to follow Grievous,<ref name="Intrigue" /> taking with him several AT-TEs. After walking several kilometers to find a non-damaged escape pod, Grievous and his troops were able to send a signal to the fleet, calling for a ship to come pick them up. However, before they could take off, the Republic army caught up to them, and the cyborg once again dueled Kenobi. Nonetheless, he was able to briefly stun the Jedi, and escape, to the chagrin of Kenobi.<ref name="The Deserter">{{TCW|The Deserter}}</ref>

====Attacking Tipoca City====
{{Quote|We must stop the production of new clones if we are to win this war.|Grievous telling Ventress of the importance of stopping clone production, in an intercepted hologram transmission|<ref name="ARC Troopers">{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:VentressFlirty-ARCTroopers.png|thumb|left|250px|Ventress displayed a flippant disrespect for Grievous's authority.]]
Sometime after the destruction of the Rishi moon outpost, Grievous and Ventress combined their forces at the behest of Count Dooku to launch another [[Battle of Kamino/Legends|surprise attack]] on Kamino. Although [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]] Kenobi and Skywalker intercepted a transmission between the two CIS commanders, this did not hamper Grievous's plans for the destruction of Kamino. When the Separatist fleet attacked the Republic blockade, he started to sacrifice his transports to protect his [[Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|command ship]]. Kenobi, knowing that the general would never sacrifice his ships idly, went into a submarine to investigate the debris from Grievous' transports. When Kenobi discovered that the debris contained [[Aqua droid/Legends|aqua droids]] were building [[Trident-class assault ship/Legends|assault craft]], he was attacked, and the assault on [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]] started.<ref name="ARC Troopers" />

While aboard of one of the assault craft, Grievous ordered his droids to kill all, no mercy, and advanced on [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC Trooper]] [[Clone Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Colt/Legends|Colt's]] units after landing. After Ventress appeared, she [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Choke|Force choked]] and stabbed the commander with her lightsaber, causing the cyborg to compliment her on her skills, a match for his own, to which Ventress replied that while Dooku may have taught Grievous how to wield a lightsaber, it does not make them equals. The two Separatists then left to take on their objectives: Ventress would attempt to acquire a sample of the clones' [[DNA/Legends|DNA]], while Grievous assaulted the clones' barracks.<ref name="ARC Troopers" />

When the general and his droids got there, they were ambushed by [[Clone cadet/Legends|clone cadets]] and troopers under Captain [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] and Commander [[Cody/Legends|Cody]]. Grievous ordered his droids to scatter the clones, but was confronted by Obi-Wan Kenobi, and the two engaged in lightsaber duel. He managed to disarm the Jedi and tried to squash him with his feet. As he moved in for the kill, he stated to Kenobi that his [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]] and Kamino were doomed. Kenobi then [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|Force pushed]] Grievous, retrieved his lightsaber and pursued the cyborg to an outside landing platform. When the general started twirling his lightsabers, one of the [[Trident (starship)/Legends|Separatist assault craft]] wrecked the platform, causing Obi-Wan to slip down into the water once again. Grievous, seeing that Kenobi was seemingly gone, escaped on a shuttle, picked up Ventress and retreated into space.<ref name="ARC Troopers" />

====Negotiating with the Wookiees====
{{Quote|Those filthy simians! We don't have time to wait. Help them decide—send the droids!.|Grievous, to the Separatist meeting|<ref name="Deep forest">{{StoryCite|story=Deep Forest|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
[[File:Grievous_Holo.png|thumb|right|150px|Grievous commanded Nute Gunray to send the droid to Kashyyyk.]]
Eighteen months after the Battle of Geonosis, Grievous was involved in an attempt to get the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] of Kashyyyk on the Separatists' side. While Nute Gunray hoped to appeal to the lack of defenses on the planet as a reason to join them, Grievous had been growing tired of the negotiations and ordered for droids to be deployed on the planet, making a surprise attack and hoping for a hostile takeover. Grievous's plans backfired when his droids were discovered and destroyed by the Wookiee guards, but not before killing the king's son, Rikummee. These events in turn caused Kashyyyk to stand against the Separatists and join the Republic instead.<ref name="Deep forest" />

Sometime after these events, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Republic Senate]] and the [[Separatist Senate/Legends|Separatist Parliament]] [[Republic financial reform bill/Legends|debated]] on escalating the war and pursuing peace. After the Separatist Parliament decided to pursue peace, Grievous was secretly ordered by Count Dooku to deposit a group of [[Infiltrator/Demolition droid|droids disguised as sanitary units]] on Coruscant to conduct [[Bombing of Coruscant's central power distribution grid/Legends|acts of sabotage]]. Grievous gathered the droids and ordered them to proceed. Grievous's units were successful in destroying the Coruscant power generators, and the peace movement was thwarted.<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref> Not long after, Grievous was in charge of a strike force directed at Mon Calamari, which the Republic halted at [[Iceberg Three]].<ref name="Clone Wars Adventures">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]</ref>

====Skirmish on Naboo====
[[File:GrievousonNaboo.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous discussing his plans for Naboo with Jar Jar Binks (posing as Boss Lyonie) in a landing craft.]]
